mainTopic: Throwing across a רשות היחיד between two רשויות הרבים, and רב's rule that carrying in a covered רשות הרבים is exempt, tested against the wagons of the משכן
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. Someone throws an object from one רשות הרבים to another, with a רשות היחיד in between. If the object travels less than four אמות, he is פטור. The גמרא explains that this teaches two things: the separated public domains combine, and an object flying through the air is not treated as if it landed (קלוטה כמה שהונחה). Next רב rules that carrying four אמות in a covered רשות הרבים is פטור, because it is not like דגלי מדבר, the open-air camp of Israel. The גמרא challenges him from the wagons of the משכן: the space under them counted as רשות הרבים even though the loaded קרשים covered them. It answers that the קרשים were stacked with gaps, then does the math of wagon length and beam size and finds the gaps would be under three טפחים, so they count as closed (לבוד). This defense works only if the קרשים narrowed toward the top. רב כהנא then suggests that the wagons in question carried only the frames (אטבעי), with no beams. The גמרא rejects this because the frames sat on top of beams already loaded, so the wagon was covered anyway. The question on רב is still open at the end of the amud, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Less than four אמות means exempt
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא: if the thrown object travels less than four אמות, the thrower is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he throws it less than four cubits, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא about someone who throws from one רשות הרבים to another with a רשות היחיד in between. If the total distance is under four אמות, he is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not carry four אמות in רשות הרבים, so that חיוב is missing. He also is not liable for moving the object between domains, because it never landed in the רשות היחיד. The גמרא will next ask why this ruling needed to be taught.

phrases.english: Less than four cubits — exempt.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא about throwing from one public domain to another, across a private domain in between.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing from רשות הרבים to רשות הרבים across a רשות היחיד, less than four אמות in total, is פטור.

steps.title: What is this ruling teaching us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point this obvious-seeming ruling teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this ruling is needed, since it seems obvious. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Less than four אמות is normally פטור anyway. So the ברייתא must be hiding a חידוש, and the גמרא wants to identify it.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new חידוש the ruling of פטור in step 1 is teaching.

steps.title: Domains join and airborne is not resting
steps.stepSummary: Two lessons: the two רשויות הרבים combine, and an object in the air is not treated as if it landed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: domains combine, and we do not say that an object caught in the airspace is as if it was set down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two lessons. First, the two public domains combine into one measurement. Second, we do not say קלוטה כמה שהונחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesson one: if the distance were four אמות, he would be חייב even though a רשות היחיד split the path, because the domains combine. Lesson two: the object passing through the air of the רשות היחיד is not considered to have landed there. That is why he is פטור, and not חייב for bringing it into a רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: an object in the air is as if it was set down

steps.whatToRemember: Two lessons here: separated public domains combine for four אמות, and an object flying through the air is not treated as having landed.

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
domains combine —
phrases.notes: The two public domains count together toward four cubits.

phrases.english: and that we do not say an object caught in the air is as if it was set down.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רשויות מצטרפות, and we do not hold קלוטה כמה שהונחה.

steps.title: Carrying in a covered public domain is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that carrying four אמות in a covered רשות הרבים is פטור, because it does not resemble the open camp in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה said in the name of רב אבא, in the name of רב הונא, in the name of רב: One who carries four cubits in a covered public domain is exempt, because it is not like the flag-camps of the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new rule. Carrying four אמות in a roofed-over רשות הרבים is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of שבת domains are modeled on the camp of Israel in the מדבר, called דגלי מדבר. That camp was open to the sky. A covered area therefore does not fully match the model. It is still a public area, but this particular חיוב does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: one who carries (moves) an object along
the flag-camps of Israel in the desert

steps.confusionAlert: רב does not say a covered street stops being רשות הרבים. He only says that carrying four אמות inside it is exempt, because it lacks the open-air feature of the model.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Abba said, Rav Huna said, Rav said:
One who carries four cubits
in a covered public domain — is exempt,
because it is not similar to the flag-camps of the desert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement on a related topic: the definition of רשות הרבים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying four אמות in a covered רשות הרבים is פטור, since it does not resemble דגלי מדבר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the details of the desert camp define the boundaries of liability for carrying in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: But the space under the wagons was covered
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: the wagons of the משכן were covered by the beams, yet רב himself said the space under them was רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the wagons were covered, and רב said in the name of רבי חייא: wagons — beneath them, between them, and at their sides is public domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. The wagons carrying the קרשים were covered, yet רב himself said the area under them counted as רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The space under a beam-loaded wagon is a covered space. If that space was still רשות הרבים in the desert model, then covering should not matter. That contradicts רב's ruling in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: beneath them, between them, and at their sides

phrases.english: Is that so?! But the wagons were covered,
phrases.notes: The loaded beams formed a roof over the wagon.

phrases.english: and Rav said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya:
Wagons — beneath them, between them, and at their sides
is public domain!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a covered רשות הרבים is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the wagons was covered, yet it was רשות הרבים, so covering should not exempt.

steps.title: The beams were stacked in rows with gaps
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רב meant that the beams were arranged in stacks with gaps between them, so the wagon was not fully covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב said this, it was about beams arranged in stacks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the קרשים lay in separate stacks with open spaces between them. So the area under the wagon was not truly covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gaps open to the sky existed between the stacks, the space below was not a covered area. That removes the contradiction with רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: in rows or stacks (with spaces between)
when he said it, he meant

phrases.english: When Rav said it, it was regarding stacks (arranged with gaps).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the wagons were not fully covered).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wagons were completely roofed by the beams.
steps.terutzMaskana: The beams were in separate stacks with open gaps, so the space under the wagon was not covered.

steps.title: The gaps are too small and count as closed
steps.stepSummary: The math: a 5-אמה wagon holds three stacks of 1.5-אמה beams, leaving only half an אמה. Split into gaps, that is less than three טפחים each, so לבוד closes them.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, how long was a wagon? Five cubits. How wide was a beam? A cubit and a half. How many did one place? Three. Half a cubit is left over. When the Master spreads it between the stacks, it is considered לבוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 6 using numbers. The gaps would be too small to matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three stacks at 1.5 אמות each take up 4.5 of the 5 אמות. That leaves half an אמה, which is 3 טפחים, spread over the gaps. Each gap is under 3 טפחים, so the rule of לבוד treats it as closed. The wagon would count as fully covered after all.

keyTerms.meaning: a gap under 3 טפחים is treated as closed

steps.confusionAlert: לבוד means that a gap smaller than three טפחים is viewed as solid. So small gaps do not open the roof.

phrases.english: After all, how much was the length of a wagon —
five cubits;
how much was the width of a beam —
a cubit and a half;
how many could one place — three;
half a cubit remains;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שָׁדֵי לֵיהּ מָר בֵּינֵי וּבֵינֵי —
phrases.english: when the Master spreads it in between —
it is considered לבוד (closed)!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that gaps between the stacks left the wagon uncovered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The leftover space is too small, so by לבוד the gaps count as closed and the wagon is covered.

steps.title: The beams lay on their narrow side
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the קרשים were placed on their thickness (1 אמה), not their width, so they took up less room and left bigger gaps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think they placed the beams on their width? They placed them on their thickness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the beams stood on their narrow side. Each stack took up only one אמה instead of 1.5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the orientation changes the math. Narrower stacks leave more open space on the wagon, so the gaps might be large enough to avoid לבוד.

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ קְרָשִׁים אַפּוּתַיְיהוּ הֲוָה מַנַּח לְהוּ?
phrases.english: Do you think one would place the beams on their width?
One would place them on their thickness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ קְרָשִׁים אַפּוּתַיְיהוּ הֲוָה מַנַּח לְהוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting a factual assumption about how the beams were placed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each stack took up only 1 אמה, leaving more open space.

steps.title: Even on their thickness the gaps are too small
steps.stepSummary: Even on their 1-אמה thickness, four stacks fit and leave one אמה. Split into gaps, that is still under three טפחים each, so it is לבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ultimately, how thick was a beam? A cubit. How many would one place? Four. A cubit is left. When the Master spreads it in between, it is considered לבוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא redoes the math with the new answer and finds the same problem. The gaps are still too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four stacks of 1 אמה fill 4 of the 5 אמות, leaving one אמה, which is 6 טפחים. Spread over three gaps, that is 2 טפחים each, still under 3. So לבוד applies again, and the wagon counts as covered.

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף סוּמְכָא דְקֶרֶשׁ כַּמָּה הָוֵי — אַמְּתָא,
phrases.english: Ultimately, how much was the thickness of a beam — a cubit;
how many would one place — four;
a cubit remains;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שָׁדֵי לַהּ מָר בֵּינֵי וּבֵינֵי,
phrases.english: when the Master spreads it in between,
it is considered לבוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף סוּמְכָא דְקֶרֶשׁ כַּמָּה הָוֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that placing the beams on their thickness leaves real gaps.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One אמה over three gaps gives 2 טפחים each, under 3, so it is still לבוד.

steps.title: It works if the beams narrowed toward the top
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the קרשים were an אמה thick at the bottom and narrowed to a fingerbreadth at the top, the gaps on that end are wide enough, so רב works.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says the beams were a cubit thick at the bottom and narrowed at the top to a fingerbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a partial solution. If the beams tapered, the gaps at the narrow end are large, and the wagon was not covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the narrow end, each beam is only a finger thick. That leaves gaps well over 3 טפחים, so לבוד does not close them. The space under that part of the wagon was open, and רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: this works for the one who says

phrases.english: This works for the one who says
the beams at the bottom were a cubit thick,
and at the top they narrowed down to a fingerbreadth —
it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 9 according to one opinion only.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limited resolution, valid only according to one view of the beams' shape.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The beams were a uniform thickness, so the gaps were under 3 טפחים.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the beams tapered, the gaps at the narrow end exceed 3 טפחים and there is no לבוד.

steps.title: But if the beams were thick throughout
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the קרשים were an אמה thick at the top as well, the gaps remain לבוד, and the question on רב stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says that just as they were a cubit thick at the bottom, so too at the top they were a cubit thick, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the problem again according to the other view, where the beams never narrowed. It asks how רב can be defended. The next step gives רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the beams were a full אמה thick all along, the gaps stay at 2 טפחים, which is לבוד. The space under the wagon would then be covered, yet still רשות הרבים. That again contradicts רב's ruling.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
just as at the bottom their thickness was a cubit,
so too at the top their thickness was a cubit,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּלְּמַטָּן עוֹבְיָין אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the resolution of step 10 fails according to the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a covered רשות הרבים is פטור, according to the view of uniformly thick beams.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With uniform 1-אמה beams, the gaps are לבוד, so the area under the wagon was covered yet was רשות הרבים.
steps.whatToRemember: The defense of רב works if the קרשים tapered at the top. The next step answers this challenge.

steps.title: רב כהנא: it refers to wagons carrying only the frames
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that רבי חייא's statement refers to wagons carrying only the אטבעי (frames), not the קרשים, so the space under them was uncovered רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It is talking about the frames!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a new answer to defend רב after the math showed the gaps would be לבוד. He says that רבי חייא's ruling (the area under the wagons is רשות הרבים) refers to wagons carrying only the אטבעי (frames), with no קרשים loaded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last attack worked because stacks of קרשים would fill the wagon and leave gaps under three טפחים. רב כהנא changes the picture: רבי חייא was speaking about a wagon carrying only the אטבעי, with no beams on it. Such a wagon was not covered, so the area beneath it was an ordinary, uncovered רשות הרבים, and there is no contradiction with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Frames or supports that held the beams in place on the wagon
Public domain, the area the סוגיא is trying to establish under or between the wagons

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: With the frames!
phrases.notes: רבי חייא's ruling is about wagons carrying just the frames, before any beams were loaded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by limiting רבי חייא's statement to wagons carrying only frames.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: רבי חייא's ruling refers to wagons carrying only the frames, without beams.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the wagon was loaded with stacks of קרשים, which leaves only tiny gaps that are לבוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is about a wagon carrying only the אטבעי, without beams, so the area under it was uncovered רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The frames sat on the wagon, so it was covered anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the frames were placed and answers itself: on top of the wagon. So the wagon was still covered, and רב כהנא's answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where were the frames placed? On the back of the wagon. So the wagon itself was covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא by asking where these frames actually were. It answers its own question: on the back of the wagon. That means the wagon was covered after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's answer needs a wagon that carried frames without beams. But the frames were placed on top of the wagon only after the קרשים were already stacked on it. So whenever the frames were there, the wagon was already covered (מקורה) by the beams, and the difficulty from step 11 returns.

keyTerms.meaning: On the back (top) of the wagon

steps.confusionAlert: The question and answer here are both said by the גמרא in one breath. It is not a new opinion. It is a single rhetorical move that knocks down רב כהנא's answer.
steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא tried to defend רב with the frames (אטבעי). The גמרא rejects this because the frames sat on the wagon, so the wagon was covered. The question on רב is still open here, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: The frames, where would they place them?
phrases.notes: The גמרא tests רב כהנא's answer.

phrases.english: On the back of the wagon,
phrases.notes: The גמרא answers its own question.

phrases.english: so the wagon itself was covered.
phrases.notes: The beams beneath the frames already covered the wagon, so there was never a beam-free wagon with frames on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks and rejects רב כהנא's answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that the frames left the wagon area open.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The frames were placed on top of the wagon after the beams were already loaded, so the wagon was covered by the beams whenever the frames were on it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There was never a wagon carrying only frames. The frames rested on top of beams already stacked on the wagon, so it was covered.
